title: CMS to Publish Medicaid AI Fraud Pilot Results, Expand Provider Exclusions
source_used: Nextgov/FCW (original); pool item was ExecutiveGov's relay of it
key_facts: Kimberly Brandt, CMS Deputy Administrator, spoke at the ADAPT conference in Santa Fe, New Mexico, on Thursday (15 Oct 2026).

CMS will soon publish results of an Indiana Medicaid fraud pilot run with Oracle and is working with five other states on pilots; the pilots use AI to flag upcoding, phantom services and geographic anomalies in near real time before payment.
A new exclusion authority granted by HHS earlier this week lets CMS bar providers from Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE and other federal programmes; Brandt hopes suspensions quadruple over six months.

CMS slideshow: technology-enabled programme integrity efforts credited with $41.9 billion in fiscal 2025 savings, a 59% rise; the Medicaid War Room (launched April 2026) stopped $342 million in improper payments and sent 124 notices of intent to exclude providers as of Sept. 2026.
A 'Netflix-type algorithm' compares new providers with existing ones; suspect ones go on a six-month watchlist and about 67% of those have been cut for non-compliance.

Brandt acknowledged 'there are a lot of things about WISeR that are not working', a six-year AI-supported prior-authorisation pilot that hospitals and Democratic lawmakers say delays and denies seniors' care; the House Ways and Means Committee advanced a provision to end it in June, the Senate has rejected such efforts.
quote_evidence: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services plans to expand provider suspensions and publish the results of a pilot testing whether artificial intelligence can prevent Medicaid fraud, a senior agency official said Thursday.
Brandt said CMS will soon publish the results of an Indiana Medicaid fraud pilot the agency conducted with Oracle, and that it is also actively working with five other states on Medicaid pilots.
“There are a lot of things about WISeR that are not working,” Brandt said
why_it_matters_hint: CMS is betting on AI to stop Medicaid fraud before payment and on new power to expel providers, but the results are not yet public.
notes: Pool link was ExecutiveGov, which cites Nextgov/FCW; read the Nextgov/FCW original (decoded via Google News) and credited it. Savings figures are CMS's own.
